name: Causal Bisimulation for Model-Call Identity
research_question: Does the current Trigger-2 model-call binding identify an execution occurrence, or only a content-equivalence class, and what identity split is required so exact replay can remain idempotent without collapsing genuinely distinct model-call events?

hypotheses.claim: The current CLAY_TRIGGER2_MODEL_CALL_BINDING/v2 digest is a content identity, not a sufficient causal occurrence identity, because it omits causal_event/admission/route/plan/cell/attempt identity.

A two-level identity split—model_call_content_digest plus model_call_event_id—can preserve deterministic replay while separating distinct executions that happen to have identical bound content and output.

counterhypotheses.claim: The existing digest is intentionally content-addressed and an enclosing repository-bound receipt already provides occurrence identity, so no change to the call-level ABI is necessary if downstream consumers always bind that enclosing occurrence receipt.
Adding event identity directly to model_call_identity may over-fragment semantic equivalence classes and weaken useful replay deduplication unless content identity remains separately preserved.

cross_connections: PR-1891 distinct-execution versus semantic-replay identity law
falsifier: If current downstream NODE_RESULT/J-Space/evaluation lineage is proven to bind a separate immutable call-occurrence receipt containing causal_event_id/admission_id/route/grid-cell/attempt identity and rejects same-occurrence/different-content conflicts, then the call-level occurrence gap is already closed outside the digest and this field reduces to a naming/documentation clarification.
